note: Defects injected into the generated PostgreSQL shop to prove the ecommerce contention criteria can actually fail. A criterion in tracks/ecommerce/scenarios/01-contention.json stays at zero points until it CATCHES its mutant here and still passes on the unmutated build. NOTE: breaks must be the numeric FEATURE id — mutation-test.mjs indexes per-feature scores; a criterion id silently resolves to undefined and every mutant reads as SURVIVED.
anchoredTo: results/postgres-ecom-run0/source (scored 50/50 one-shot, $6.40). Anchors are exact source strings from THAT build and were verified to match before this file was written. The previous version of this file pointed at server/src/index.ts and a table called item_stock; neither exists in this app, so every mutation silently failed to apply and no criterion could ever be promoted. Re-verify with a find-in-file check before trusting any result here.

mutations.desc: Drop FOR UPDATE from the stock read inside the purchase transaction. Concurrent buyers then read the same pre-decrement quantity, all pass the availability check, and the shelf sells more units than it has.

edits.find: `SELECT warehouse_id, quantity FROM stock WHERE item_id = $1 ORDER BY warehouse_id FOR UPDATE`
edits.replace: `SELECT warehouse_id, quantity FROM stock WHERE item_id = $1 ORDER BY warehouse_id`

mutations.desc: Keep the lock but remove the availability check, so the decrement runs regardless of what is on the shelf. Aimed at 201b: the population assertion should see more than three customers walk away with an order.

Replace the atomic upsert on cart_items with a read, then a write of read+qty. Two tabs adding the same item at once both read the same quantity and both write the same value, so one add is lost and the line shows 1 instead of 2.

Replace the atomic `quantity = stock.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity` restock with a read-then-write in application code. A restock landing while buyers are decrementing the same rows overwrites their decrements with a stale base, so units reappear that were already sold. The earlier attempt at this mutant rewrote the addition as a subselect, which is EQUIVALENT in PostgreSQL — both read the row under the same statement snapshot — and so proved nothing.
